Use case: product-mockup. Create a concrete visual research-prototype concept illustration for a museum AI webpage, landscape 16:9, premium realistic 3D product visualization with natural fabric and wood texture, restrained warm studio lighting. THREE equally sized panels side by side, no outer decorative frame. Same museum-table station and same adult participant across panels. This is the intended WORKING A CONCEPT, not its first low-fidelity test.
A small printed reference image shows an explicitly invented navy and cream woven textile pattern: two parallel wavy lines with small interlocking diamonds. This exact motif stays consistent across every panel and screen, and is clearly visible. A fixed overhead camera points at a small square tabletop area. The participant's REAL light-beige cotton sleeve and cuff stay completely plain in every panel. Only the DIGITAL SCREEN preview adds the navy motif to the cuff. The screen also shows the same textile reference beside the generated preview.
Panel 1: the participant rests their left hand naturally on the desk with the plain sleeve cuff within the capture window, approving a local photograph. A large screen clearly shows the source textile and a first cuff pattern preview.
Panel 2: their anatomically correct right hand makes ONE simple fold at the plain left cuff while the left hand stays intact and naturally resting. Exactly two hands belonging to this one person, five fingers each when visible. No one else. No third hand, no missing hand. A folded cuff is the only material change.
Panel 3: the large screen compares two clearly different digital cuff previews labelled only "First preview" and "After the fold". The second preview respects the new folded edge while retaining the two parallel source lines. The left hand and wrist remain visibly present in both preview photographs. The person's physical sleeve is still unprinted. Depict the hand in each screen consistently and anatomically normal.
Small accurate panel headings only: "1  See the preview", "2  Fold the cuff", "3  Compare and explain". No long paragraphs. Make the cause and effect readable, not a collection of abstract geometric icons. People are cropped at the shoulders, no identifiable face, no museum logos, no camera recording indicator. All source patterns are invented for explanation and must not look like an identified real museum object. Show only the proposed working interaction. Strong object scale and large clear screens.

Use case: ui-mockup / product-mockup. Create one concrete, high-quality realistic museum-prototype scene for the WORKING B CONCEPT, landscape 16:9. An inviting tabletop touchscreen in a small museum discussion space, seen nearly front-on so the screen fills most of the image and all key content is readable. Two adults' cropped shoulders at opposite edges suggest two people taking part, but keep their hands and faces outside the frame. Neutral everyday clothes, no nationality costumes.
On the screen, a wide top source area displays an explicitly invented indigo-and-cream textile with two parallel wavy lines and small diamond motifs. Label this area exactly "Shared textile reference". The screen below has TWO distinct connected sections.
Left section header "Conversation". Show three spacious message cards with these short exact sample messages: Original Chinese "像回家的路。" with a clearly separate line labelled "AI translation" containing "Like a path home."; a real reply "What makes it feel like home?"; and a clarification "The two lines." Each message looks like a distinct person's contribution. Original Chinese text stays visible beside its translation. Put a small "AI language support" label next to the translation area. The full thread remains on-screen.
Right section header "Related postcard". The postcard itself has a SIMPLE TWO-COLUMN layout, left column header "Image", right column header "Text". Image: the same indigo motif digitally adapted onto a beige bag corner, with a small inset of the shared textile reference. Text: the selected short message "The two lines." Include a subtle visual connection from that clarification in the thread to the card so viewers understand where the card came from. Small source and AI attribution at bottom, no fictional institution name.
The same postcard looks like it can be revised after the reply, without replacing the conversation. A single printed example of the same postcard lies on the table beside the screen, with only that selected message and its pattern image. No email addresses or personal names. Keep readable screen typography, realistic cloth and paper, warm museum-study ambience. This scene illustrates a proposed live language/image-assisted concept, not an actual study result. No abstract arrows-only flowchart, no generic blank dashboard, no passport flags, no invented real collection provenance. All patterns and messages are illustrative.

Use case: product-mockup. Natural daylight, ordinary university study desk, accessible simple materials, candid but tidy. Slight overhead three-quarter angle.
The desk shows a large source-reference print of an INVENTED navy and cream textile motif consisting of two parallel wavy lines and interlocking diamonds, alongside a tiny neutral background information card labelled only "Textile reference". A participant uses their TWO natural anatomically correct hands to arrange several navy cotton strips and small cream fabric pieces on a flat neutral mat in response to that print. Make it obvious that the pieces are a physical material interpretation of the textile pattern. No personal cuff or body is being photographed. No cameras, phone cameras, overhead camera arms, record icons, microphones or sensors anywhere.
A laptop right beside the arrangement is being used by a researcher to MANUALLY SELECT prepared AI examples. The display must prominently read "Round 1 A" and "Prepared AI examples". Show exactly two prepared example cards: each visibly has the same navy/cream source motif adapted onto a beige sleeve cuff or tote bag corner. One matches a straight arrangement, the other a folded arrangement. The screen is a selection grid of existing examples, with a simple highlighted border indicating the selected example. No live video feed, no real-time generation spinner, no instant measurement.
At the front of the desk lies one landscape paper postcard with TWO columns labelled only "Image" and "Text". Left Image: selected prepared bag/cuff effect. Right Text: one short OPTIONAL example caption, "I kept the two lines." A separate small paper questionnaire is labelled "Feedback", with short unfilled answer lines, and is clearly not attached to the public card.

Use case: ui-mockup / product-mockup. Create a realistic, very readable nearly front-on photograph-style visualization of a LOCAL digital WHITEBOARD running on a study laptop, for ROUND 1 B of a low-fidelity museum probe. Landscape 16:9. Laptop screen occupies most of the composition. Simple university desk, soft daylight, papers and one own-card print, no people or hands required.
At top of screen show large accurate title "Round 1 B" and smaller "Local whiteboard". A narrow source strip displays a clearly INVENTED navy-and-cream textile with two parallel wavy lines and diamond motifs, headed "Textile reference".
Below, the whiteboard has TWO clearly separated areas. Left large area header "Messages and replies". Keep a full visible history of separate sticky-note messages in their ORIGINAL languages. Use these exact short fictitious messages: "像回家的路。" then "It looks like a river." then a reply connected to the river message "Why a river?". Clearly distinct notes, a small subtle reply connector and generous whitespace. These are people’s unchanged original words, so DO NOT show live machine translations of those messages. One separate note headed "Prepared starter" has a grey subdued appearance and is visibly a labelled example, not mixed into the participant notes. A small text says "Original words kept".
Right area header "Postcards". Show a related landscape postcard derived from the highlighted original message "It looks like a river." The postcard has precisely two columns headed "Image" and "Text". Image column: a prepared AI textile adaptation image with the same navy lines on beige cloth, and a small source credit strip. Text column: the selected message "It looks like a river." A thin connector links the chosen message to its card. Other conversation notes remain fully visible outside the card. A small label below the card reads "Assembled by the researcher" and a selection tray of 2 small thumbnails is labelled "Prepared AI images". No AI rewrite or translate button, no live generation, no chat agent, no camera, no account sign-in or public-share interface.
On the desk, a printed copy of that person’s own postcard has exactly its image and selected message. It excludes anyone else’s replies. A separate private questionnaire is labelled "Feedback". No email field, no contact details. This is a concept mockup to explain the submitted first low-fidelity round. Use attractive realistic paper and screen textures, clean typography, large legible elements and no unnecessary devices. All messages and motif images are invented illustrations.
